chapters.title: Getting Started
text: Barely Functional Contraptions makes power from mushrooms, light and empty space, and grows resources on sheep.
## The machine casing
Every machine is built around a Functional Machine Block: craft it from iron ingots, copper ingots and redstone, and use it in the machine recipes.
## The loop
- Mycelial Generators burn mushrooms and water to make Forge Energy (FE).
- Infuse sheep with a resource (an iron ingot, a diamond...) at an Infusion Altar to change their wool.
- Shear them for resource wool, and turn the wool back into resources in a Mechanical Separator powered by FE.
- Mushroom sheep give the generators their fuel, which closes the loop.
Sneak and right-click a sheep with an empty hand to see what it is infused with. JEI and Jade, if installed, show recipes and machine details.

chapters.title: Wrench and Links
text: The Barely Functional Wrench links blocks without touching.
- Right-click a generator, then another generator, to link them into one network (up to 64 blocks apart).
- Right-click a generator, then a Mechanical Separator, Automatic Shears or Hume Energy Cube, to power it wirelessly.
- Sneak and right-click a block to remove its links. Sneak and right-click the air to clear your selection.
The generator's screen shows how it is connected and which machines it is powering.
The wrench also sets each side of a Fluid or Item Pipe: see Pipe Sides.

chapters.title: Data Packs
text: Sheep resources are data: data/<namespace>/barelyfunctionalcontraptions/sheep_resources/<name>.json. They reload with /reload.
An appearance block gives any resource wings, extra heads, glowing, a bigger size, its own sounds and more.

Furnace heat sources are data too: data/<namespace>/barelyfunctionalcontraptions/furnace_heat/<name>.json names a sheep, an entity or a look such as on_fire, and its power. Boost items are the blaze_furnace_boost data map.
Wool Burner fuels are data too: data/<namespace>/barelyfunctionalcontraptions/wool_burner_fuel/<name>.json, each with an ingredient, a burn_time and a power.
A separating recipe whose ingredient matches a Wool Bale (barelyfunctionalcontraptions:wool_bale with its sheep_resource component) gives that bale its own outputs instead of the scaled-up wool ones.
## Commands
- /barelyfunctionalcontraptions list: every loaded resource.
- /barelyfunctionalcontraptions generate: a resource for every material in the modpack.
- /barelyfunctionalcontraptions generate item <item>: a resource fed with any item.
Every number in the mod can be changed in its config files, from the mod list's Config button.

chapters.title: Glow Panels
text: The Glow Panel makes power from the light falling on its top.
- In full sunlight it makes 60 FE/t, less at dawn, dusk and in rain, and nothing at night.
- Under block light it makes up to 40 FE/t. A Glow Lamp on it or above it gives the full amount, day or night, even underground.
- A glowing Glow Ink sheep standing next to it lights it up too.
Its cells glow brighter the more it makes: dim at dawn, dusk or in rain, half lit under a Glow Lamp at night, fully lit in the midday sun, and dark when it makes nothing.
It pushes its energy into blocks beside and below it.
## Glow Lamp
A full-brightness lamp made from glow ink sacs, glass and glowstone dust.

chapters.title: Wool Burner
text: The Wool Burner burns spare wool for power, one item at a time.
- Plain wool (any colour): 30 FE/t for 10 seconds.
- String: 30 FE/t for 2.5 seconds.
- Coal Wool: 120 FE/t for 20 seconds.
Right-click it with fuel to load it, put fuel in the slot in its window, or feed it with a hopper or pipe. Hoppers and pipes can't take fuel back out.
It stores 20,000 FE and pushes it into every block around it. While its buffer is full it waits before lighting the next item, so nothing is wasted.
A comparator reads how full its fuel slot is.
## Data packs
Fuels are data: data/<namespace>/barelyfunctionalcontraptions/wool_burner_fuel/<name>.json, each with an ingredient, a burn_time in ticks and a power in FE/t.

chapters.title: Blaze Furnace
text: The Blaze Sheep Furnace makes power from the heat of Blaze sheep standing in the 5x5 area around it (the config's radius), on its own level or on top of it.
- One Blaze sheep gives 80 FE/t. Each extra one adds a little less: 150, 210 and 260 FE/t for two, three and four. It counts up to four.
- Only a sheep showing its blazing fleece counts. A sheared sheep or a lamb gives nothing until its wool grows back.
- In rain or water a sheep gives half.
- Right-click with a Blaze Rod to load it, or put rods in the boost slot in its window: each rod doubles the output for 30 seconds. Hoppers and pipes can fill it too.
Shear the sheep for Blaze Rods, or leave the fleece on for power: that's the trade-off.
It pushes its energy into every block around it, and a comparator reads one level per 20 FE/t.
Right-click it with an empty hand to open its window. The fire in the middle column rises with the heat; each line is one more heat source, and its pip lights while that source is in use.
## Showing the area
Click the spyglass button in the furnace's, the Automatic Shears' or the Infusion Altar's window, or sneak-right-click any of them with an empty hand, to show or hide its working area.

chapters.title: Mycelial Generator
text: Burns red or brown mushrooms and water to make FE: 200 FE/t from brown mushrooms, 250 FE/t from red ones.
## Running it
- Give it water with a bucket, a bucket in its slot, a pipe, or a Fluid Reservoir placed next to it.
- Put mushrooms in the top slot. Hoppers and pipes can insert from any side.
- It pushes energy into cables and machines next to it.
## Networks
Generators that touch form a network, and every running member boosts the whole network's output exponentially.
## Mycelium
Running generators slowly turn nearby dirt into mycelium and sometimes sprout huge mushrooms, which gives you more fuel.

chapters.title: Zero Point Module
text: Place two modules facing each other, on a floor and ceiling or on two walls, with open space between them.
- They link with a beam and make 1,000 FE/t for every block of gap, up to 64 blocks.
- Take the energy from either end.
- Stained glass in the gap colours the beam.
- The beam burns anything that walks into it, and mobs it kills drop loot as if you had killed them.

chapters.title: Energy Storage
text: A battery: 1,000,000 FE and 10,000 FE/t per cube. Touching cubes join into one bigger battery that pushes into the machines and cables around it.

chapters.title: Cables and Meter
text: ## Energy Cable
Joins generators, batteries and machines into one network moving up to 100,000 FE/t. Generators power machines first and charge cubes with the rest.
## Energy Meter

Place it between a generator or battery and what it powers: it works out which way the energy flows by itself (in at the back, out at the front). The wrench flips it. Its screens show the FE/t passing through. Right-click for the total, and read it with a comparator: the signal rises with the flow.

chapters.title: Tanks and Pipes
text: ## Fluid Tank
Holds 16 buckets of one fluid. Touching tanks join into one big tank that fills from the bottom up. Use buckets on it, or connect pipes on any side.
## Fluid Pipe
Carries fluid between anything that holds it, up to 4 buckets a tick. Machines are filled first, then tanks.
Item Pipes carry items the same way, up to 16 a tick, taking only from output slots so chests and machine inputs are never drained.

chapters.title: Pipe Sides
text: Each side where a Fluid or Item Pipe meets a block can be set up on its own with the Barely Functional Wrench.
## Modes
Right-click the plug with the wrench to cycle it:
- Normal: fills the block, and only takes from pure sources such as the Automatic Shears.
- Pull (orange): empties the block, chests and tanks included.
- Push (green): only fills the block, never takes from it.
- Off: no connection. Wrench the face of the pipe's core to turn it back on.
## Filters

Sneak and right-click the plug with the wrench to open its filter: a 3x3 grid. Click a slot holding an item, or a bucket of a fluid, to filter it there; click with nothing to remove it. Only filtered things pass that side. The grid also has a mode button and a Clear button.
Shortcut: hold an item in your other hand and right-click the plug with the wrench to add it to the filter, or remove it again.

chapters.title: Wool Packer
text: The Wool Packer presses 9 of the same resource wool into one Wool Bale. Each bale takes 1,000 FE over 2 seconds.

Right-click it with resource wool, put wool in the left slot of its window, or feed it with a hopper or pipe. The nine pips light up as the wool for the next bale comes in. Hoppers and pipes take the bales out of any side, but never the wool.
## Separating bales

Put a whole bale in the Mechanical Separator. It takes 15 times the power of one wool, more than its 9 wool would, and as long as those 9 one at a time. In return it gives 12 wool's worth of everything: a third more resources.
An Iron Wool Bale, for example, gives 24-48 raw iron and 24 string for about 300,000 FE, where its 9 wool would give 18-36 raw iron.
Bales stack to 64, so they also carry nine times as much wool in a chest or pipe.
To get the wool back, put a bale on its own in any crafting grid: it gives its 9 wool.
## As a block
A bale can be placed like a hay bale, in the colour of its wool, and softens falls the same way. Breaking it gives the bale back.
## Config
The packer's power and speed, and what bales cost and give in the separator, are in the [wool_packer] section of the server config.

chapters.title: Infusing Sheep
text: Sheep are infused at a powered Infusion Altar (see its chapter): the resource in the centre, two of its blocks and a rarity item round it, and a grown sheep standing beside it.
- Its fleece takes the resource's colour, and small blocks of the resource grow out of it.
- Each infusion lasts 100 shearings by default.
- Breed infused sheep with wheat and the lamb is born infused too.
- Kill an infused sheep with its wool for a little extra.
- In creative, the Resource Wool tab has a spawn egg for every sheep, which spawns it already infused.
Right-clicking a sheep with a resource does nothing now; wheat, dyes and shears behave as usual. A server can bring hand feeding back in the config ([infusion_altar] handFeedingMaxTier).
## More resources

Data packs can add any resource, and operators can run /barelyfunctionalcontraptions generate to make one for every metal in the modpack. Generated sheep take 2 of the block, an ingot and a Golden Carrot.

chapters.title: Themed Sheep
text: Ten resources turn sheep into little versions of the mob they come from:
- Hay Bale: a hay fleece (wheat).
- Nether Star: two Wither Skeleton Skulls beside its head (nether stars).
- Dragon's Breath: dragon wings (dragon's breath).
- Glow Ink Sac: a glowing fleece that lights up the ground (glow ink).
- Bone Block and Wither Rose: skull faces and bony legs (bones).
- Spider Eye: extra legs and red eyes (spider eyes).
- Echo Shard: sculk tendrils (echo shards).
- Blaze Rod: always on fire, but never hurt (blaze rods).
- Ghast Tear: twice the size, tentacles, and it screams like a ghast (ghast tears).
Each one has its own advancement, and collecting every wool is a challenge.

chapters.title: Infusion Altar
text: Every sheep is infused at the Infusion Altar. Put the resource in the centre slot and its catalysts in the slots round it, power the altar, and stand a grown sheep within 2 blocks of it. The sheep takes the resource when the bar fills, and the items are used up then. The altar slows the sheep down while it works, so it doesn't wander off, and lets it go once it's done.
## The recipe
Most sheep take the same pattern: the ingot (or gem, dust or item) in the centre, 2 of its blocks, and one more item for how rare the sheep is.
- Common, a Wheat: Stone, Wood, Coal, Copper, Hay, Red and Brown Mushroom.
- Uncommon, a Golden Carrot: Iron, Gold, Redstone, Lapis, Quartz, Glow Ink, Spider, Skeleton.
- Rare, a Golden Apple: Diamond, Emerald, Blaze, Ghast.
- Epic, an Eye of Ender: Netherite (with Ancient Debris), Wither Skeleton (with Nether Bricks).
For example, Iron is an Iron Ingot in the centre with 2 Blocks of Iron and a Golden Carrot. They take 20,000 FE over 5 seconds.
## Tier 2: legendary sheep
- Wither: Nether Star, with 4 Soul Sand, 2 Bone Blocks, 1 Wither Rose.
- Dragon: Dragon's Breath, with 4 End Stone, 4 Popped Chorus Fruit, 2 Eyes of Ender.
- Warden: Echo Shard, with 4 Sculk, 4 Amethyst Shards, 1 Sculk Catalyst.
Tier 2 takes 200,000 FE over 5 seconds.

The catalysts still needed show faded in the empty slots, and the Recipes tab lists every sheep's. Hoppers and pipes can feed it from any side, so it can infuse a pen without you. The spyglass button in its window, or a sneak-right-click with an empty hand, outlines the area the sheep must stand in.

When the resource and all its catalysts are in, the altar gives a one-tick redstone pulse on every side, so a dispenser or piston can bring the next sheep, or a circuit can stop the hoppers. A comparator reads its progress.
Data packs set a resource's tier, catalysts and power in its "altar" block.

chapters.title: Breeding Sheep
text: Every sheep has three stats from 1 to 10. Wild sheep are all 1s.
- Yield: more wool per shearing. Yield 10 gives about 2.35 times as much.
- Growth: sheared wool grows back on its own, without grass. At Growth 10 it takes about 11 seconds.
- Endurance: an infusion lasts more shearings. Endurance 10 makes it last 1.9 times as long.
A lamb gets the average of its parents' stats, with a 1 in 4 chance of each going up one (and a small chance of one down). Keep breeding your best sheep together to push a line up.
Sneak and right-click a sheep with an empty hand to see its stats, or look at it with Jade.
Lambs of infused sheep are born infused too, and their own Endurance counts.

chapters.title: Wool Machines
text: ## Mechanical Separator
Put resource wool in and supply FE. Each wool gives 2 to 4 of its resource, 2 string and sometimes a bonus. Iron wool takes 20,000 FE over 5 seconds.
Its redstone button sets whether redstone turns it on or off. Hoppers and pipes can feed it and empty it.
It also separates Wool Bales from the Wool Packer, for more resources (see Wool Packer under Logistics).
## Automatic Shears
Shears every sheep in the 3x3 area in front of its blades, using 2,000 FE per sheep, and keeps the wool in 9 slots. Put a hopper or pipe under it to collect the wool.

chapters.title: Fluid Reservoir
text: Place it on top of an infinite water source and it fills with a bucket of water a second, which it pushes into tanks and generators beside it.

chapters.title: Work in Progress
text: Features still being built are written up here as they arrive, so you can see what's coming.

Here are the planned late-game generators, which make a lot of power but need looking after, and the Quantum Sheep. None of them can be built yet, and their numbers may change. Back up your world before trying anything here once it arrives.

chapters.title: Hume Field Generator
text: Planned. Not in the game yet; the numbers may change.
A paired machine that isn't sure whether it makes power. Its output follows the infused sheep in its observation pen, whether they're watched or not.
## Power
- Around 10,000-60,000 FE/t on average, but it jumps around from moment to moment.
## Upkeep
- Smooth it out with a bank of Hume Energy Cubes, or the swings are hard to use.
- Re-infuse the sheep in its pen regularly, or its output averages down.

chapters.title: Echo Chamber
text: Planned. Not in the game yet; the numbers may change.
A Warden sheep in a sculk-lined room. The chamber turns the sheep's vibrations into energy.
## Power
- Around 20,000 FE/t, more while it's noisy nearby.
## Upkeep
- Keep the noise steady: note blocks, a redstone clock, or a Wool Burner's crackle.
- Too quiet and the Warden sheep falls asleep and it stops. Too loud and the room shrieks, then stops for a cooldown.
- The sculk catalysts in the room wear out and need replacing.

chapters.title: Lightning Array
text: Planned. Not in the game yet; the numbers may change.
A tall copper mast, barely grounded, that catches lightning and stores it.
## Power
- Each strike gives a huge burst, around 5,000,000 FE, into Hume Energy Cubes that drain it out slowly.
## Upkeep
- It only works in thunderstorms, unless you call a strike with a Trident or a Charged Creeper head.
- Each strike oxidises the mast one stage. Scrape it with an axe or wax it; fully oxidised, it stops working.
- Sheep near a strike become Charged sheep with a crackling fleece, worth more in the Mechanical Separator.

chapters.title: Fleece Fusion
text: Planned. Not in the game yet; the numbers may change.
Fuses two different resource wools into power, such as Iron and Gold, or Coal and Netherite.
## Power
- Set by the pair: from about 5,000 FE/t for common pairs up to 50,000 FE/t for Dragon and Warden.
- The pairs and their power will be data, like Wool Burner fuels.
## Upkeep
- A steady flow of resource wool or Wool Bales, so it keeps a sheep farm busy.
- Lint builds up in its chamber. Clear it out with shears every so often; it comes out as plain wool for the Wool Burner.

chapters.title: Quantum Sheep
text: Planned. Not in the game yet; how it works may change.
A sheep that isn't sure whether it exists. Nobody is quite sure what it's infused with either, least of all the sheep.
## What it does
- Now and then it blinks out of existence for a few seconds, then pops back a few blocks away, or in the same place as if it never left.
- Each time it comes back, its wool may have changed to another resource at random.
- Shear it and every piece of wool can be a different resource, so one shearing can give Iron, Diamond and Coal Wool at once.
## The catch
- You can't choose what it gives, and the rarer resources turn up less often.
- It can't be relied on for an Automatic Shears farm: if it isn't there when the blades come round, nothing is sheared.
- Breeding two Quantum Sheep might give a Quantum lamb, a normal sheep, or both and neither.
